If you want all of your legend labels in italics you can use legend.text in the options. 

http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Legend-Attributes

/shameless self-promotion

#usage
plot + opts(legend.text = theme_text(face = 'italic'))

It's really hard to make out what you mean by two legends though. Usually if there are two legends it's because you have defined two separate scales (color, shape, size, linetype...). You can make them disappear, but I'm not sure if you can just combine legends. 

Brandon

Hi:

Is this perhaps (close to) what you wanted?

p1<-ggplot(tab,aes(ct,ccb,colour=espécie,shape=sexo))
q1 <- p1 + geom_point(size=2.5) + scale_shape("Sexo") +
     labs(x="Comprimento padrão (cm)", y="Comprimento côndilo-basal (mm)") +
     opts(legend.position="none")
p3 <- ggplot(tab, aes(ccb, lr, colour=espécie, shape=sexo))
q2 <- p3 + geom_point(size=2.5) + scale_shape("Sexo") +
     labs(x="Comprimento côndilo-basal (mm)",y="Largura rostral (mm)") +
     opts(legend.text=theme_text(face ="italic"))

grid.newpage()
vp1 <- viewport(width = 0.4, height = 1, x = 0.2, y = 0.5)
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.6, height = 1, x = 0.7, y = 0.5)
print(q1, vp = vp1)
print(q2, vp = vp2)

The page rendering uses the grid package; the code is a modification of the examples in section 8.4 of Hadley's book. The warnings will tell you that the observations with missing values are deleted from the plot.

Hi:

Thanks to Luciano and Ista for pointing me in the right direction - I had done some searching of the list archives but hadn't found what I needed. The following replacement seems to work for the q2 plot:

q2 <- p3 + geom_point(size=2.5) + scale_shape("Sexo") +
     labs(x="Comprimento côndilo-basal (mm)",y="Largura rostral (mm)") +

scale_colour_hue(breaks = levels(espécie),
              labels=parse(text=c(paste('italic("',unique(espécie)[1:2],'")'))))

Substitute this into my earlier script and hopefully that gets what Daniele wanted.

Dennis
